questions.question: Who was the chief guest at India’s 76th Republic Day parade in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prabowo Subianto**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India** invited **Prabowo Subianto**, the **President of Indonesia**, to be the **Chief Guest** for the **76th Republic Day** parade held on **January 26, 2025**.
 
• This invitation marks a significant milestone in the **bilateral relations** between **India** and **Indonesia**, particularly as both nations are celebrating **75 years** of established **diplomatic relations** in **2024-2025**.
 
• **Prabowo Subianto**, who took office as the **8th President of Indonesia** in **October 2024**, made his first official state visit to **India** during this event, reinforcing the **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership** signed in **2018**.
 
• The **Republic Day** parade, held at **Kartavya Path** in **New Delhi**, serves as a platform to showcase India's **military strength**, **cultural heritage**, and **technological advancements** to the global community.
 
• The choice of an **Indonesian** leader is historically symbolic, as **President Sukarno** was the first-ever **Chief Guest** at India's very first **Republic Day** celebrations in **1950**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India-Indonesia Strategic Ties:**
 
 
• **India** and **Indonesia** share deep maritime boundaries and are key partners in the **Indo-Pacific** region.
 
• The **"Act East Policy"** of India considers **Indonesia** a vital pillar for regional stability and **maritime security**.
 
• Economic cooperation is robust, with **Indonesia** being India's largest trading partner in the **ASEAN** region, particularly in the trade of **palm oil**, **coal**, and **crude petroleum**.
 
 
 
• **Recent Chief Guests:**
 
 
• In **2024** (the **75th Republic Day**), the Chief Guest was **Emmanuel Macron**, the **President of France**.
 
• In **2023**, the Chief Guest was **Abdel Fattah el-Sisi**, the **President of Egypt**.
 
• During the years **2021** and **2022**, there were no foreign Chief Guests due to the **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
 
 
• **Republic Day Significance:**
 
 
• **Republic Day** commemorates the date on which the **Constitution of India** came into effect on **January 26, 1950**, replacing the **Government of India Act (1935)**.
 
• The date **January 26** was chosen because it was on this day in **1930** that the **Indian National Congress** proclaimed **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Defense Cooperation:** India and Indonesia regularly conduct joint military exercises, including **Garuda Shakti** (Army) and **Samudra Shakti** (Navy), to enhance **interoperability**.
 
• **Geopolitical Context:** The invitation to **Prabowo Subianto** highlights India's focus on the **Global South** and its commitment to strengthening ties with **Southeast Asian** neighbors amid changing **geopolitical dynamics** in the **Indo-Pacific**.
 
• **Cultural Connection:** The two nations share a "shared heritage," with influences of **Ramayana** and **Mahabharata** deeply embedded in **Indonesian culture** and art forms.
</ul

questions.question: The Indian hockey legend PR Sreejesh was recognized with what specific prestigious honour by President Droupadi Murmu on 28 April 2025, at Rashtrapati Bhavan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Bhushan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The legendary Indian hockey goalkeeper **PR Sreejesh** was conferred with the **Padma Bhushan**, India's **third-highest civilian award**, by **President Droupadi Murmu**.
 
• The ceremony took place at the **Rashtrapati Bhavan** on **28 April 2025**, recognizing his "distinguished service of high order" to the nation in the field of **Sports**.
 
• **PR Sreejesh** is widely regarded as one of the greatest goalkeepers in the history of field hockey, often referred to as "**The Wall of India**" for his exceptional defensive skills.
 
• The award acknowledges his immense contribution to the resurgence of **Indian Hockey** on the global stage, particularly his role in securing consecutive **Olympic medals**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Padma Bhushan.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Career Profile of PR Sreejesh:**
 
 
• Born in **Kizhakkambalam**, **Kochi**, **Kerala**, Sreejesh made his debut for the **Senior National Team** in **2006** at the **South Asian Games** in **Colombo**.
 
• He served as the **Captain** of the **Indian Men's Hockey Team** during the **2016 Rio Olympics** and the **2016 Champions Trophy**, where India won a historic **Silver Medal**.
 
• He played a pivotal role in India winning the **Bronze Medal** at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics**, ending a **41-year** Olympic medal drought for Indian hockey.
 
• He concluded his illustrious **18-year-long career** after winning another **Bronze Medal** at the **Paris 2024 Olympics**, where he was celebrated for his heroic saves against **Great Britain** and **Spain**.
 
 
 
• **Awards and Recognition:**
 
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:** He received India's highest sporting honor in **2021**.
 
• **Padma Shri:** He was previously honored with the **fourth-highest civilian award** in **2017**.
 
• **Arjuna Award:** Recognized for his outstanding achievement in sports in **2015**.
 
• **World Games Athlete of the Year:** He became only the second Indian athlete to win this global title in **2021**.
 
• **FIH Goalkeeper of the Year:** He won this prestigious international award consecutively in **2021** and **2022**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Padma Awards Hierarchy:**
 
 
• The **Padma Awards** are announced annually on the eve of **Republic Day** (**26 January**).
 
• **Padma Vibhushan:** Awarded for exceptional and distinguished service (2nd highest).
 
• **Padma Bhushan:** Awarded for distinguished service of high order (3rd highest).
 
• **Padma Shri:** Awarded for distinguished service in any field (4th highest).
 
 
 
• **Post-Retirement Role:**
 
 
• Following his retirement in **2024**, **Hockey India** retired the **Jersey Number 16** in the senior men's team as a tribute to him.
 
• He was subsequently appointed as the **Head Coach** of the **India Junior Men's Hockey Team** to nurture the next generation of players.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: For which sports has Murlikant Rajaram Petkar received Arjuna Awards (Lifetime) for his outstanding performance in the year 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Para-Swimming**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Murlikant Rajaram Petkar** was conferred with the **Arjuna Award (Lifetime)** in **2024** for his legendary contributions and outstanding performance in **Para-Swimming**.
 
• He holds the prestigious distinction of being **India’s first Paralympic Gold Medalist**, achieving this feat at the **1972 Summer Paralympics** held in **Heidelberg, Germany**.
 
• Petkar won the **Gold Medal** in the **50m Freestyle Swimming** event, clocking a then-world record time of **37.33 seconds**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Para-Swimming is correct.***
 
• Initially a **boxer** in the **Indian Army**, he switched to swimming and other para-sports after sustaining permanent disabilities during the **1965 Indo-Pak War**.
 
• His life story and struggles were brought to mainstream cinema through the **2024 biopic** titled **"Chandu Champion"**, starring **Kartik Aaryan** and directed by **Kabir Khan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Military Background:**
 
 
• Petkar served as a **jawan** (soldier) in the **Corps of Electronics and Mechanical Engineers (EME)** of the **Indian Army**.
 
• During the **1965 war against Pakistan**, he sustained multiple **bullet wounds** (specifically **9 bullets**), one of which remained lodged in his spine, leading to paraplegia.
 
 
 
• **Versatility in Sports:**
 
 
• Apart from **Para-Swimming**, he was a versatile athlete who competed in **Javelin Throw**, **Precision Javelin Throw**, and **Slalom**.
 
• In the **1972 Paralympics**, besides his gold in swimming, he also reached the finals in **Javelin** and **Slalom** events.
 
 
 
• **Previous Recognitions:**
 
 
• In **2018**, the **Government of India** honored him with the **Padma Shri**, the country's fourth-highest civilian award, for his pioneering role in Indian para-sports.
 
• He was also employed by **TELCO** (now **Tata Motors**) in **Pune** for many years after his retirement from active sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Arjuna Award Context:**
 
 
• The **Arjuna Award** is usually given to athletes for consistent outstanding performance over **four years**. However, the **Lifetime** category or special recognition for legends like Petkar in **2024** highlights the government's effort to honor pioneers who were overlooked in the past.
 
• The awards are presented by the **President of India** at the **Rashtrapati Bhavan**.
 
 
 
• **The 1972 Heidelberg Paralympics:**
 
 
• These were the **4th Paralympic Games**. India finished **24th** in the medals tally out of 42 nations, solely due to Petkar's individual performance.
 
• Petkar's gold remained the only **Paralympic gold** for India for several decades until the **2004 Athens Games**.

questions.question: In July 2025, two high-speed unmanned aerial targets were successfully destroyed using the Akash Prime weapon system in which Union Territory of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ladakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Akash Prime** weapon system successfully intercepted and destroyed two high-speed unmanned aerial targets during trials conducted in **July 2025**.
 
• The successful engagement of these targets took place in the Union Territory of **Ladakh**, which provides a challenging high-altitude environment for testing advanced missile systems.
 
• **Akash Prime** is an enhanced version of the existing **Akash** missile system, specifically upgraded to provide higher reliability and better performance in mountainous terrains.
 
• The system is equipped with an indigenous **active Radio Frequency (RF) seeker**, which significantly improves the accuracy and hit probability of the missile against targets with low radar cross-sections.
 
• The testing in **Ladakh** validates the system’s operational capability near the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**, where air defense is critical due to geographical complexities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Akash Missile System**:
 
 
• The **Akash** is a **Short-Range Surface-to-Air Missile (SRSAM)** system developed by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**.
 
• It has an operational range of approximately **25 km** to **30 km** and can engage multiple targets simultaneously in all-weather conditions.
 
• The system is manufactured by **Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL)** and **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)**, representing a hallmark of the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative.
 
 
 
• **Union Territory of Ladakh**:
 
 
• **Ladakh** was established as a separate Union Territory on **31st October 2019**, following the enactment of the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019**.
 
• It is strategically located, sharing borders with **Tibet** (China), **Gilgit-Baltistan** (Pakistan-occupied), and the Indian state of **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• The region is known for its extreme cold temperatures and high altitudes, such as the **Khardung La** pass, which exceeds **17,000 feet** in elevation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technical Advancements**: The **Akash Prime** includes improvements such as a **modified ground system** and an **improved seeker** compared to the baseline **Akash** missile.
 
• **Operational Readiness**: Testing at altitudes above **15,000 feet** is crucial to ensure that the solid-fuel motors and electronic components of the missile function correctly in low-oxygen and sub-zero temperature environments.
 
• **Strategic Significance**: The deployment of such indigenous systems in **Ladakh** strengthens the Indian Armed Forces' defensive posture against aerial threats, including drones, fighter jets, and cruise missiles.
 
• **International Standing**: India has also begun exporting the **Akash** missile system to friendly foreign nations, such as **Armenia**, showcasing the global competitiveness of Indian defense technology in the **year 2024-25**.

questions.question: Which national team secured its first-ever title at the 2025 IIHF Women’s Asia Cup held in Al‑Ain, UAE?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Philippines**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Philippines** women's national ice hockey team created history by winning the **2025 IIHF Women’s Asia Cup** title.
 
• The tournament was held in **Al-Ain, United Arab Emirates (UAE)**, concluding on **January 5, 2025**.
 
• In the final match, the **Philippines** defeated **Iran** with a decisive score of **4-0** to claim the gold medal.
 
• This victory marks the **first-ever championship title** for the **Philippines** in an **International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF)** sanctioned continental tournament.
 
• The Philippine team maintained a dominant performance throughout the event, remaining **undefeated** across all their matches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tournament Branding and Scope:**
 
 
• The **2025 IIHF Women’s Asia Cup** is the newly rebranded version of what was formerly known as the **IIHF Challenge Cup of Asia**.
 
• The event aims to promote ice hockey in **Asian** and **Middle Eastern** regions where the sport is still developing.
 
 
 
• **Participating Teams and Rankings:**
 
 
• The **2025** edition featured competitive teams including **Iran**, **Japan**, **India**, **Kuwait**, and the host nation **UAE**.
 
• **Iran** secured the **silver medal**, showcasing their rapid progress in the sport after entering international competition only a few years ago.
 
• **Japan**, participating with a **development squad** (B-team), took home the **bronze medal** after defeating the **UAE** in the third-place playoff.
 
• While **China** is a major powerhouse in Asian ice hockey, they typically compete in higher **IIHF World Championship** divisions and did not field a team for this specific **Asia Cup** development tier.
 
 
 
• **Key Performers:**
 
 
• The Philippine victory was bolstered by exceptional performances from goalie **Rosalyn Lim**, who recorded a **shutout** in the final.
 
• Forwards such as **Bianca Cuevas** were instrumental in the offensive play that led the team to the **gold medal**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF):**
 
 
• The **IIHF** is the worldwide governing body for ice hockey, based in **Zurich, Switzerland**, and manages international tournaments and the **World Ranking** system.
 
 
 
• **Growth of the Sport in the UAE:**
 
 
• The **Al-Ain Ice Rink**, where the tournament was held, is a premier facility in the **United Arab Emirates**, reflecting the country's investment in winter sports despite its desert climate.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Rankings:**
 
 
• The victory in **January 2025** is expected to significantly boost the **Philippines'** standing in the **IIHF Women's World Ranking**, helping them qualify for higher-tier global competitions in the future.

questions.question: Under what theme was the International Day for Biological Diversity celebrated in 2025?

options.text: Harmony with Nature and Sustainable Development
Biodiversity: Food, Water and Health for All

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harmony with Nature and Sustainable Development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Day for Biological Diversity (IDB)** is an annual event celebrated globally on **May 22** to promote conservation and raise awareness about the vital importance of biodiversity.
 
• For the year **2025**, the theme **"Harmony with Nature and Sustainable Development"** has been chosen to emphasize the interconnectedness of human progress and environmental health. ***Hence, the correct answer is Harmony with Nature and Sustainable Development.***
 
• This theme aligns with the broader goals of the **United Nations Decade on Ecosystem Restoration (2021–2030)**, highlighting that sustainable development cannot be achieved without protecting the earth's biological variety.
 
• The **2025** focus encourages nations to integrate **biodiversity-friendly practices** into economic planning and infrastructure projects to ensure that development does not come at the cost of the natural world.
 
• It supports the ongoing implementation of the **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF)**, which serves as a strategic roadmap to halt and reverse nature loss by the **year 2030**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History and Origin:**
 
 
• The **International Day for Biological Diversity** was first established by the **Second Committee of the UN General Assembly** in **late 1993**.
 
• Initially, it was observed on **December 29** to mark the date the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)** came into force.
 
• In **December 2000**, the **UN General Assembly** officially shifted the date to **May 22** to commemorate the adoption of the text of the Convention on **May 22, 1992**, at the **Nairobi Final Act**.
 
 
 
• **The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD):**
 
 
• The **CBD** is a legally binding treaty with three main goals: **conservation of biological diversity**, **sustainable use** of its components, and the **fair and equitable sharing** of benefits arising from genetic resources.
 
• It was opened for signature at the **Earth Summit** in **Rio de Janeiro** in **June 1992**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Biodiversity:**
 
 
• Biodiversity includes the variety of **plants, animals, and microorganisms**, as well as the **genetic differences** within species and the variety of **ecosystems** (such as deserts, forests, and wetlands).
 
• Current data from the **United Nations** suggests that about **1 million species** are currently threatened with extinction, more than at any other time in human history.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Past Themes:**
 
 
• The theme for **2024** was **"Be part of the Plan"**, which was a call to action for all stakeholders to support the implementation of the **Global Biodiversity Framework**.
 
• The **2023** theme was **"From Agreement to Action: Build Back Biodiversity"**, celebrating the successful negotiations at **COP15**.
 
 
 
• **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF):**
 
 
• Adopted in **December 2022**, this landmark agreement includes **4 global goals** and **23 targets** to be achieved by **2030**.
 
• The most notable target is the **"30x30" target**, which aims to protect **30%** of the world’s **land and 30% of its oceans** by the year **2030**.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• Biodiversity conservation is a core component of several **United Nations SDGs**, most notably **Goal 14 (Life Below Water)** and **Goal 15 (Life on Land)**.
 
• It also impacts **Goal 2 (Zero Hunger)** and **Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation)** as healthy ecosystems are essential for food and water security.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Who among the following was sworn in as the Chief Justice of India on 24 November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surya Kant**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• Justice **Surya Kant** is designated to be sworn in as the **Chief Justice of India (CJI)** on **24 November 2025**. 
• He will succeed Justice **B.R. Gavai**, following the established convention of **seniority** in the **Supreme Court of India**. 
• Justice **Surya Kant** was elevated as a **Judge of the Supreme Court** on **24 May 2019**. Prior to his elevation to the apex court, he served as the **Chief Justice** of the **Himachal Pradesh High Court**. 
• His tenure as the **Chief Justice of India** is expected to last until **9 February 2027**, when he reaches the mandatory retirement age of **65 years**. 
• Born on **10 February 1962** in **Hisar, Haryana**, he has had a distinguished legal career, including serving as a **Judge** of the **Punjab and Haryana High Court** for over a decade. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Appointment of the CJI**: 
• The **Chief Justice of India** is appointed by the **President of India** under **Clause (2)** of **Article 124** of the **Constitution**. 
• The outgoing **CJI** recommends the name of the **senior-most judge** of the **Supreme Court** as their successor, a convention that is almost always followed except in rare historical instances. 
• **Other Notable Personalities in the Options**: 
• **N. V. Ramana**: Served as the **48th Chief Justice of India** from **April 2021** to **August 2022**. 
• **D. Y. Chandrachud**: Served as the **50th Chief Justice of India**, with a two-year tenure ending in **November 2024**. 
• **Ranjan Gogoi**: Served as the **46th Chief Justice of India** and was the first **CJI** from the **North-Eastern region** of India. 
• **Role and Functions**: 
• The **CJI** is the **head of the judiciary** of India and the **Supreme Court**. 
• As the **Master of Roster**, the **CJI** has the exclusive prerogative to constitute benches and allocate cases to the judges of the court. 
• The **CJI** also heads the **Collegium**, which recommends names for the appointment of judges to the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Constitutional Provisions**: **Article 124** to **Article 147** of the **Constitution of India** deal with the organization, independence, jurisdiction, powers, and procedures of the **Supreme Court**. 
• **Retirement Age**: Unlike **High Court** judges who retire at **62**, **Supreme Court** judges, including the **CJI**, hold office until they attain the age of **65 years**. 
• **Oath of Office**: The **CJI** is administered the **oath of office** by the **President of India** as per the **Third Schedule** of the **Constitution**. 
• **First CJI**: **H. J. Kania** was the first **Chief Justice of India** after the **Constitution** came into effect in **1950**. </ul

questions.question: Which of the following three-city groups emerged as the top ‘Swachh Shehar’ in the (more than 10 lakhs population) Swachh Survekshan 2024-25 awards hosted by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ahmedabad, Bhopal, Lucknow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swachh Survekshan 2024-25** marks the **10th edition** of the world's largest urban sanitation survey, launched to foster a spirit of healthy competition among cities to improve service delivery to citizens.
 
• In the category of cities with a population of **more than 10 lakhs** (Million-plus cities), the group of **Ahmedabad**, **Bhopal**, and **Lucknow** emerged as the top performers based on the latest assessment parameters.
 
• The **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)** oversees the survey, which evaluates cities on various parameters such as **segregation of waste at source**, **processing of wet and dry waste**, and the **remediation of legacy dumpsites**.
 
• **Ahmedabad**, located in **Gujarat**, has been a consistent leader in **Solid Waste Management** and has previously secured **7-star Garbage Free City** ratings.
 
• **Bhopal**, the capital of **Madhya Pradesh**, has frequently been recognized as the **Cleanest State Capital**, focusing on **citizen-led initiatives** and **sustainable waste processing**.
 
• **Lucknow**, in **Uttar Pradesh**, has shown remarkable progress in **urban cleanliness** by integrating **Smart City** technology with waste collection monitoring.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of Swachh Survekshan:**
 
 
• The survey was first conducted in **2016** covering **73 cities**. By **2024**, it has expanded to cover more than **4,500 cities** across India.
 
• It is the primary monitoring tool for the **Swachh Bharat Mission - Urban (SBM-U)**, which was launched on **2nd October 2014**.
 
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission 2.0:**
 
 
• Launched in **October 2021**, **SBM-U 2.0** aims to make all Indian cities **'Garbage Free'** and **'Water Plus'** over the next five years.
 
• The mission focuses on **100% source segregation**, **door-to-door collection**, and **scientific processing** of all fractions of waste.
 
 
 
• **Assessment Methodology:**
 
 
• The survey methodology is data-driven and includes **Service Level Progress (SLP)**, **Certification** (Star Rating for Garbage Free Cities), and **Citizen Voice**.
 
• **Citizen Voice** is a crucial component that collects feedback from millions of residents regarding the cleanliness of their respective cities.
 
 
 
• **Key Themes:**
 
 
• Each year, the survey adopts a theme, such as **'Waste to Wealth'** for 2023 or **'Clean Cities, Healthy Lives'** for the 2024-25 cycle.
 
• The **2024-25** edition emphasizes the **circular economy**, where waste is treated as a resource rather than a liability.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **GFC Star Rating:** This is a protocol designed by **MoHUA** to grade cities on a **1, 3, 5, and 7-star** scale based on their cleanliness and waste management efficiency.

questions.question: Where did President of India Droupadi Murmu launch India’s first home-grown anti-cancer CAR-T cell therapy?

options.text: All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Institute of Technology Bombay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The President of India, **Droupadi Murmu**, launched India’s first home-grown **CAR-T cell therapy** on **April 4, 2024**.
 
• The launch took place at the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay**, located in **Mumbai**, **Maharashtra**.
 
• This therapy, named **NexCAR19**, is the first **indigenously developed** gene therapy for cancer in India.
 
• The development of this treatment is a collaborative milestone involving **IIT Bombay**, the **Tata Memorial Hospital**, and the industry partner **ImmunoAdoptive Cell Therapy (ImmunoACT)**.
 
• During the event, the **President** highlighted that the development of this therapy is a testament to the **"Make in India"** initiative and a step towards **"Atmanirbhar Bharat"** in the high-tech healthcare sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NexCAR19 Therapy:**
 
 
• It is a **Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell (CAR-T)** therapy, often referred to as "living drug" because it uses the patient's own immune system to fight cancer.
 
• The therapy is primarily used to treat **B-cell lymphomas** and **B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia** in patients where conventional treatments like chemotherapy have failed.
 
• **NexCAR19** works by genetically modifying a patient’s **T-cells** to express a receptor that can specifically target and kill cancer cells.
 
 
 
• **Cost and Accessibility:**
 
 
• Internationally, **CAR-T cell therapy** is extremely expensive, costing around **$400,000 to $500,000** (approx. **₹3 crore to ₹4 crore**).
 
• The Indian-made **NexCAR19** is expected to be available at about **one-tenth** of the international cost, making it significantly more affordable for Indian patients.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Milestones:**
 
 
• The **Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)** granted market authorization for **NexCAR19** in **October 2023**.
 
• This approval followed successful clinical trials that demonstrated high efficacy and a lower side-effect profile compared to existing international versions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scientific Leadership:** The research was led by **Dr. Rahul Purwar** and his team at the Department of Bioscience and Bioengineering, **IIT Bombay**.
 
• **Global Standing:** With this launch, **India** joins an elite group of nations (including the **USA** and **China**) that possess the capability to produce indigenous **CAR-T cell therapies**.
 
• **Government Support:** The project received significant funding and support from the **Department of Biotechnology (DBT)** and the **Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC)** under the **National Biopharma Mission**.
 
• **Future Scope:** While currently approved for specific blood cancers, researchers are working on expanding the application of **CAR-T cell therapy** to treat other types of cancers and autoimmune diseases in the **year**s to come.

• In **May 2025**, regional tensions led to an engagement where **India** utilized its advanced **BrahMos** missile system against **Pakistan**. This event highlights the strategic importance of high-speed precision weaponry in modern conflict scenarios. ***Hence, the correct answer is Pakistan.***
 
• The **BrahMos** is a **supersonic cruise missile** that was developed as a joint venture between **India's Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** and **Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya (NPOM)**.
 
• This missile system is highly regarded as one of the **fastest cruise missiles in the world**, operating at speeds of **Mach 2.8 to 3.0**, which is nearly three times the speed of sound.
 
• The **BrahMos** operates on the **"Fire and Forget"** principle, meaning it does not require further guidance after launch to hit its designated target with extreme precision.
 
• The missile's name is a combination of two major rivers: the **Brahmaputra** of **India** and the **Moskva** of **Russia**, symbolizing the bilateral cooperation between the **two countries**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Initially, the range of the **BrahMos** was capped at **290 km** to comply with the **Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR)** guidelines.
 
• Following **India's** entry into the **MTCR** in **June 2016**, the range has been successfully extended to **450 km** and even **800 km** in newer variants.
 
• The missile can be launched from multiple platforms, including **land-based mobile launchers**, **ships**, **submarines**, and **Su-30 MKI fighter aircraft**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• In **March 2022**, a **BrahMos** missile was accidentally fired from **India** into **Pakistan** due to a technical malfunction during routine maintenance, landing near **Mian Channu**.
 
• The **Indian Air Force (IAF)** conducted a high-level inquiry into the **2022** incident, leading to the termination of three officers for deviating from Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
 
 
 
• **Global Export and Demand:**
 
 
• The **BrahMos** missile has gained international attention, with the **Philippines** becoming the first foreign country to sign a deal worth **$375 million** to acquire the shore-based anti-ship variant in **January 2022**.
 
• Several other nations in **Southeast Asia** and the **Middle East** have expressed interest in the missile system due to its **low radar signature** and high lethal power.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Significance:** The deployment and use of **BrahMos** by **India** serves as a major deterrent, providing the **Indian Armed Forces** with a significant "stand-off" range capability.
 
• **Warhead Capacity:** The missile can carry a conventional warhead weighing between **200 and 300 kilograms**, depending on the launch platform and specific mission requirements.
 
• **Flight Ceiling:** It can fly at altitudes as low as **10 meters** (sea-skimming) to avoid detection or as high as **15 kilometers**.
</ul

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, during its **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** meeting concluded in **June 2025**, announced a strategic decision to cut the **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** by **50 basis points (bps)**.
 
• This reduction of **50 bps** (which is equivalent to **0.50%**) is aimed at augmenting the liquidity available within the banking system to support economic growth and ensure smoother credit flow.
 
• By lowering the **CRR**, the **RBI** effectively reduces the amount of cash that commercial banks are mandated to keep with the central bank, thereby increasing their **lendable resources**.
 
• The move was influenced by the need to maintain an "accommodative" or "neutral" stance depending on the prevailing **inflation** and **GDP growth** dynamics observed in the first quarter of the **financial year 2025-26**.
 
• This **50 bps** cut is expected to release a significant amount of primary liquidity into the financial markets, helping banks manage their **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** more efficiently without increasing the cost of funds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**:
 
 
• It refers to the share of **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** that banks must maintain as a cash balance with the **RBI**.
 
• Crucially, banks do not earn any **interest** on the money kept as **CRR**, making it a powerful tool for the **RBI** to control the **money supply** in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Basis Points (bps)**:
 
 
• In financial terminology, **1 basis point** is equal to **1/100th of 1%** or **0.01%**.
 
• Therefore, a **50 bps** cut represents a **0.50%** reduction, while a **100 bps** cut would represent a full **1%** change.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**:
 
 
• The **MPC** is a **six-member** committee constituted by the **Central Government** under **Section 45ZB** of the amended **RBI Act, 1934**.
 
• The committee is chaired by the **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India** and is tasked with determining the policy rates required to achieve the **inflation target** (typically **4%** with a band of **+/- 2%**).
 
 
 
• **Impact of CRR Cut**:
 
 
• A lower **CRR** results in a higher **Money Multiplier**, as banks have more capital to lend to consumers and businesses.
 
• This usually leads to a decrease in **lending rates** (like **MCLR** or **EBLR**), making loans for housing, automobiles, and industrial expansion more affordable.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**: While **CRR** is kept in cash with the **RBI**, **SLR** is the reserve that banks must maintain in the form of liquid assets like **Gold** or **Government Securities** before they can provide credit.
 
• **Repo Rate**: This is the rate at which the **RBI** lends money to commercial banks in the event of any shortfall of funds. It is the primary signal rate for the economy.
 
• **Liquidity Management**: The **RBI** uses instruments like **Open Market Operations (OMO)**, **CRR**, and the **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)** to manage the volume of money in the **Indian economy**.
 
• **Historical Context**: **CRR** levels have historically fluctuated between **3% and 15%** depending on the economic cycle and the **RBI’s** objective to either suck out excess liquidity (inflation control) or inject liquidity (growth stimulus).
